summary: Discovery on balancing latency, cost and compliance across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Focus areas: fast region steering, active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs, KV cache warmup and priming strategies, SLA mapping and partial degradation policies, incident playbooks for cache loss and model fallbacks.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~9 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (Head of Platform - Capstone), Tom Nguyen (CTO - Capstone), Priya Shah (SRE Lead - Capstone)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda 1 understand your production constraints, 2 talk reliability patterns across Hosted / Dedicated / Private, 3 pilot next steps.
[00:12] Elena: thanks. we shipped inference last quarter and have pain points around regional outages and cold starts on our KV caches.
[00:25] Tom: our main ask 1 keep sub-200ms p95 for auth flows and degrade gracefully for non-critical paths; also EU-only data residency for some products.
[00:36] Raj: are you running active-active or active-passive across regions today?
[00:40] Priya: active-passive with DNS failover. DNS TTLs aren't cutting it for latency SLOs. we tried global LB but costs spiked.
[00:49] Maya: common tradeoff. Redwood recommends traffic steering with fast region cutover plus canary failover to alternate region or lower-cost model variant.
[00:58] Elena: model variant meaning 8-bit/quantized? what's the quality delta?
[01:03] Raj: quantized or lighter model proxy. delta depends on prompts; we'll bench with your sample prompts.
[01:12] Tom: KV cache warmup is big for us 1 spikes when nodes are cold during failover. priming approach?
[01:18] Raj: two approaches: passive priming from recent traffic and active prefilling during planned failovers. active-active with KV replication keeps caches warm but needs dedicated capacity and replication bandwidth.
[01:30] Priya: how much extra capacity does that use? finance will push back on doubling GPU spend.
[01:35] Maya: Hosted reduces your ops burden; Redwood manages multiplexing and has cold-cache mitigations. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lets you provision standby capacity for warm caches but costs more committed spend. we'll include a cost comparison.
[01:52] Elena: SLA mapping: what SLAs do you offer and how do you handle partial degradation?
[01:57] Maya: Dedicated customers typically get 99.9% plus latency SLOs per route; hosted tiers up to 99.5 depending on plan. For partial degradation we support policy-driven fallthroughs: canary to alternate model, regional steering, capacity-tier fallback like batching or non-streaming.
[02:16] Tom: need p95 latency in contract. can you attach p95 objectives?
[02:20] Raj: yes, we can include p95 latency objectives per route for Dedicated. typical trimmed gen p95 numbers are 100-200ms on T4-equivalent shapes; we'll test with your token lengths.
[02:33] Priya: maintenance windows and auditability? our SOC team wants audit logs for model rollouts and kernel selection changes.
[02:38] Maya: Private deployments give most control 1 full audit logs, customer-managed upgrades, and KMS/HSM integration. Hosted provides audit logs too but vendor-managed. we'll share audit log sample and KMS guide.
[02:55] Elena: air-gapped on-prem constraints? we have a regulated product needing air gap for data at rest.
[03:00] Raj: we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped installs, supports HSMs and internal-only networking; longer procurement and support path.
[03:09] Tom: can you simulate switching a region and estimate user-visible error rate for chaos tests?
[03:14] Maya: yes, pilot includes chaos scenario matrix: region outage, node degradation, model rollout regression. SE will run ramp tests and report p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
[03:25] Raj: we'll model fallback policies 1 immediate cutover vs traffic-split ramp (e.g., 90/10) and show token-cost and latency curves.
[03:36] Priya: do you have an ops playbook for regional KV cache loss and degrading to a lighter model?
[03:40] Maya: yes, ops playbook covers detection (tail latency, cache-miss rate), circuit-break thresholds, automated routing to fallback, alerting, and postmortem templates; we'll include a sanitized example.
[03:55] Elena: SSO and RBAC needs 1 SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[03:59] Raj: console supports SAML SSO and SCIM; Dedicated/Private can enforce org RBAC and ship logs to your SIEM.
[04:08] Tom: model regression after rollout 1 is there automatic rollback?
[04:12] Raj: yes, canary and A/B with automatic rollback triggers on quality regressions you define; tie alarms to traffic steering.
[04:22] Priya: for the pilot we need a test plan with chaos scenarios and a checklist of sample data and credentials you'll need.
[04:27] Maya: noted. Raj will define the bench harness.
[04:31] Raj: I'll draft a harness that runs your prompts across regions and models, collects latency, token cost, quality metrics, includes KV priming step and simulated failover.
[04:45] Tom: timeline 1 pilot in June, move to Dedicated by Q4 if successful, budget in Q3.
[04:52] Maya: we'll propose a 6-8 week pilot with success criteria: <200ms p95 for auth path during normal ops and limited degradation (<10% latency increase) during simulated regional outage for non-critical flows.
[05:08] Elena: vendor lock-in concerns 1 portability of models and prompts?
[05:12] Raj: models aren't locked; you can pin versions and export binaries for self-hosting in Private. some runtime optimizations are Redwood-specific. prompts and app code remain yours.
[05:22] Priya: support during incidents 1 24/7?
[05:25] Maya: Dedicated customers get 24/7 on-call and a named SE for the pilot; Hosted has business-hours support with escalation.
[05:34] Tom: example failure: region A loses 70% capacity for 10 minutes, walk through.
[05:38] Raj: detection via p99 and error rate, automated steering to region B with ramp, if B under-provisioned fallback to quantized model for non-critical calls and pin critical calls to standby capacity, warm caches via prefilling, alert ops and open incident.
[05:58] Elena: do you map user-visible errors distinct from internal errors?
[06:02] Raj: yes, we instrument both and will show impact as failed user transactions for your auth path.
[06:12] Maya: recap and next steps: send SOC2 + KMS guide, Raj drafts harness + topology diagram, propose pilot dates.
[06:25] Priya: we'll prepare sample traffic profile and prompt list for quality evaluation.
[06:30] Tom: thanks, looking forward to bench results.
[06:33] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule.
[06:37] [Call ends]

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-typed proper nouns (Red wood / K M S) and minor speaker attribution uncertainty; left conversational artifacts intact.
